newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU, US to resume veterinary pact talks on Dec 18.
newsitem.headline: EU, US to resume veterinary pact talks on Dec 18.

text.p: The European Union and United States are due to resume negotiations for an agreement on the mutual recognition of veterinary standards on December 18, an Irish EU presidency official said on Thursday.
"It's not impossible that agreement could be reached," the official said, adding that the meeting in Brussels was scheduled to last two days. The last round of talks ended on December 6.

If there is no deal, providing sufficient progress had been made, there could be a "gentleman's agreement" under which the EU would extend current import arrangements for up to three months, the official said.
The Farm Council may discuss the issue when it holds a monthly meeting on December 16-17.

Washington has been concerned that an estimated $2.0 billion trade in veterinary and phytosanitary products could be disrupted when the EU harmonises import rules in the 15 member states on January 1, 1997, resulting in stricter standards.
The EU move is part of efforts to complete a single internal market.

Imports of U.S. petfood and other meat products could be blocked due to stricter EU controls against Bovine Spongiform Encephalopathy (BSE), while shipments of other products would be subject to closer inspection, delay and extra cost.
Washington could raise the issue at an EU-U.S. summit meeting in Washington on December 16.
